Internal_Reference.comment: (instance_id=nkd5015 serial_number=3500015), (instance_id=nkd5017 serial_number=3500017) Due to its proven reliability and ability to withstand the ionizing radiation and thermal stresses of low Earth orbit, NASA has integrated unmodified D5 units into its standard flight kit for the International Space Station (ISS) and astronaut training at Johnson Space Center. The Artemis II mission carried two Nikon D5 cameras that were used by the crew as the primary handheld cameras for lunar flyby observations with improved ability for human-eye observations through the long lens over more modern mirrorless cameras.

(instance_id=1104 serial_number=22238223), (instance_id=1105 serial_number=22238221) The HOBO MX1101 by Onset Computer Corporation is a compact, battery-powered data logger that measures and records ambient temperature and relative humidity. On Artemis II, two were used to measure temperature, dew point, and relative humidity to characterize the storage compartments (Lockers D/E) within Orion throughout the mission, informing future sample return storage conditions.

instance_id=nkz9019 serial_number=3920019 Continuing the Nikon legacy in space exploration, the Z9 serves as the technical core of the Handheld Universal Lunar Camera (HULC) for future Artemis missions, where its specialized firmware and hardware modifications manage the intense ionizing radiation and thermal fluctuations of the lunar environment.
The Artemis II mission carried one Nikon Z9 camera that was used by the crew for shortlens imaging during the mission and for performance testing for use on future Artemis missions.

(instance_id=pcd1), (instance_id=pcd2), (instance_id=pcd3), (instance_id=pcd4) The Portable Computing Device (PCD) is a Microsoft Surface Pro 5 tablet used by the Artemis II crew members during the mission. Artemis II carried four PCD tablets during the mission (PCD1, PCD2, PCD3, and PCD4). The primary uses of the PCD were 1) to record audio recordings of crew observations as captured by the Peltor Headset and PCD Audio Recorder), 2) record handwritten crew notes/observations, 3) serve as an imagery relay so that imagery can be downlinked during the mission to the flight control team and 4) provide the Lunar Target Guide to support lunar observations.

Instrument_Host.name: Artemis 2 Orion spacecraft
Instrument_Host.description: The Orion spacecraft (named Integrity by the Artemis II crew) is NASA's deep-space vehicle designed to carry and support up to four astronauts as part of the Artemis program's return to the Moon. The spacecraft consists of the U.S. Crew Module and European Service Module, together equipped with life support systems, radiation protection, heat shield, propulsion system with 33 engines, and deep space communications and navigation.
